title: Design System: Arif Rahman Mubarok — Personal Site

display.purpose: The hero name only, authored as two fixed lines so it never wraps unpredictably.

head.purpose: One per section — the section's own title.

figure.purpose: The five stat numbers in Numbers only; carries tabular-nums and the decimal-align logic.

lead.purpose: The hero's supporting sentence and other single statements heavier than body copy.

body.purpose: All running text: bios, ledger detail, bullets, coupon copy. Kept at 17px or above everywhere.

small.purpose: Metadata only — ledger highlight/year, stat captions, cert issuer/date, footer credits.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Per-element scroll entrance: opacity 0→1, translateY(24px)→0, staggered by a --reveal-delay custom property.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: The signature slow-zoom move on the Showcase server-rack photograph.

motion.name: pan
motion.purpose: The one other moving picture: a slow horizontal pan on the batik textile band in Credentials.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Flat Ledger Cobalt fill, Folder Sand text, square corners. 'Let's connect' / 'View repo'.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; background: #062b8a; color: #e6dbc7; padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { opacity: 0.85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #062b8a; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The inverse of Primary — Folder Sand fill, Ledger Cobalt text — for a second action on a cobalt ground.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; background: #e6dbc7; color: #062b8a; padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover, .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { opacity: 0.85; }

components.name: Folder Tab
components.description: Signature component: the hero's section links as a stack of peeking file-folder bands with trapezoid tabs.
components.html: About↓Numbers↓
components.css: .ds-folder-stack { position: relative; width: 86%; margin: 0 auto; } .ds-folder { position: relative; display: block; min-height: 84px; padding: 20px 24px; color: #062b8a; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 300ms ease; } .ds-folder:hover, .ds-folder:focus-visible { transform: translateY(-8px); } .ds-folder-tab { position: absolute; top: -18px; left: 24px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 34px; padding: 0 16px; background: #062b8a; color: #e6dbc7; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; clip-path: polygon(0 100%, 0 0, 100% 0, 85% 100%); } .ds-folder-arrow { position: absolute; bottom: 16px; right: 24px; opacity: 0.4; font-size: 13px; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-folder:hover .ds-folder-arrow { opacity: 0.9; }

components.name: Ledger Row
components.description: A job-history row: company, one-line highlight, year range, and a circular +/- expand control. Real conditional render, not CSS-hidden.
components.css: .ds-ledger-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; width: 100%; min-height: 44px; padding: 20px 0; background: transparent; border: none; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; color: #062b8a; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-ledger-row:hover { opacity: 0.7; } .ds-ledger-company { font-size: 19px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-ledger-highlight { flex: 1; font-size: 14px; color: #2a4a8f; } .ds-ledger-year { font-size: 14px; color: #2a4a8f; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-ledger-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #d3c4a6; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Stat Row
components.description: One quantified proof point: a decimal-aligned figure (fixed-width whole part, left-aligned suffix) and a caption.
components.html:
50

invoices batched into a single IRB e-Invoice submission
components.css: .ds-stat { padding: 20px 0; } .ds-stat-figure { display: flex; align-items: baseline; } .ds-stat-whole { width: 5ch; text-align: right; font-size: 64px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #062b8a; } .ds-stat-suffix { text-align: left; font-size: 64px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #062b8a; } .ds-stat-caption { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 17px; color: #2a4a8f; }

components.name: Scalloped Sheet
components.description: The About/Credentials panel: a fixed-width Manila sheet with a scalloped bottom edge, used for the letter and the credentials menu.
components.html:
A letter, from Jakarta

I'm a Software Engineer based in Jakarta…
components.css: .ds-sheet { position: relative; max-width: 640px; padding: 48px 40px; background: #ddd0b9; color: #062b8a; } .ds-sheet::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: -1px; height: 22px; background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 11px 0, #e6dbc7 11px, transparent 11.5px); background-size: 22px 22px; background-repeat: repeat-x; } .ds-sheet-title { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-sheet-body { margin-top: 28px; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.55; }

components.name: Coupon
components.description: The Contact card: a cobalt coupon with top/bottom semicircle notches and a dotted perforation between the pitch and the form.
components.html:
Let's connect

I usually reply within 24 hours.
components.css: .ds-coupon { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; max-width: 896px; background: #062b8a; color: #e6dbc7; } .ds-coupon::before, .ds-coupon::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 46%; width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #e6dbc7; } .ds-coupon::before { top: -14px; } .ds-coupon::after { bottom: -14px; } .ds-coupon-pitch, .ds-coupon-form { padding: 48px; } .ds-coupon-pitch h2 { font-size: 32px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-coupon-pitch p { margin-top: 32px; font-size: 17px; } .ds-coupon-form input { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 52px; margin-bottom: 10px; padding: 0 16px; background: #e6dbc7; color: #062b8a; border: none; font-size: 17px; }

narrative.overview:
The site is built as the physical object its subject's own specialty would produce: a stack of filed folders you open through, and a ledger of figures and roles. The hero isn't a banner with a nav bar bolted on — the six section names *are* folder tabs, peeking out of a stack on a cobalt letterhead ground, with the front one already open. The idea traces straight back to the one fact that makes this candidate specific: he batches Malaysia's e-Invoice submissions and exports database records for a living, so the page itself is stationery — a letter, a ledger, a menu sheet, a coupon — not a generic component kit wearing his name.

Density follows the object it's imitating: the hero's folder stack is tight and tabbed, the ledger rows in "Where I've worked" are compact until opened, and the stat column reads like figures ruled into a page. Between those, full-bleed real pictures (an archival account-book cover, a 19th-century batik textile, a server rack, a muted typing loop) carry the "paper and ink" world further without ever standing in for a product shot he doesn't have. The palette is two tones doing every job: one cobalt ink, one sand paper, nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: The page's own object-ness carries the identity: folders, scalloped letter sheets, a ledger table, a clip-out coupon, each a flat shape with real cut edges, never an outlined box.
One typeface (Switzer), one hue (Ledger Cobalt) against one paper tone (Folder Sand) and its two tonal steps (Manila, Manila Deep).
Every section is a structurally different composition from its neighbor; nothing repeats as a card grid.
Real, credited pictures of the subject's world appear at least once per section that has room for one, duotoned into the palette.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: The entire palette is Ledger Cobalt plus the Folder Sand/Manila family — no third hue, no tint derived from opacity. A new "lighter" or "muted" value is one of the two named tones or Muted Cobalt; it is never invented as rgba(ink, 0.4).

rules.name: The Reversal Rule
rules.body: Depth and hierarchy come from which surface is cobalt and which is sand, not from shadow or tint. A component never mixes the two directions; pick one reversal per surface.

rules.name: The Decimal-Align Rule
rules.body: Each stat's value is split at the first non-digit character into a whole part (right-aligned, fixed 5ch width) and a suffix/decimal part (left-aligned), so 3.7/4.0 sits in the same ruled column as 1,000+ without hand-kerning.

rules.name: The Five-Step Rule
rules.body: Display, Head, Figure, Lead, Body, Small — six named roles, but Figure only ever appears in one section. Every inline literal size should resolve to one of these.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to look above another, it changes tone or changes which color is ground vs. ink — never a box-shadow, including as hover feedback on interactive elements.

rules.name: The Cut-Edge Rule
rules.body: When a section boundary needs interest, the edge itself is shaped (a tab, a scallop, a notch, a dotted perforation) rather than decorated with a border, divider, or shadow.

dos: Do keep the palette to exactly Ledger Cobalt, Muted Cobalt, Folder Sand, Manila, Manila Deep — five named values, no opacity-derived tints.
Do give every real photograph the shared .duotone filter before placing it; an un-toned photo breaks the one-world premise immediately.
Do shape an edge (tab, scallop, notch, perforation) when a section boundary needs interest; never reach for a border or shadow.
Do keep running text at Body size (17px+) or larger; Small is for metadata only.
donts: Don't reintroduce dark mode or a second theme — the object this page imitates has one ink, one paper, in the physical world.
Don't add a shadow anywhere, including as hover feedback; color/opacity only.

Don't use native <details>/<summary> for the next collapsible pattern without checking it first — the rendering environment used for this build did not hide closed-details content, which silently broke two inspector checks until the Ledger Row was rewritten as a real conditional render.
Don't add a sixth type-size step; fold a new size need into the nearest existing one first.
